editorial.headline: Payment Services: A Clear National and Bali Route for Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the customer-facing infrastructure of payments, from payment accounts and remittances to acquiring and payment gateways.
editorial.body:
Payment Services Provision is the front-end work of making a payment system usable for its end users. It covers the administration of payment funding sources, including the issuance of payment instruments or payment accounts; the transmission of fund-transfer instructions, including remittance services; and the transmission of payment-transaction data. In practice, its scope reaches the customer-facing functions around displaying funding-source information, initiating transactions, acquiring, electronic wallets, payment accounts, fund transfers and payment gateways.

It is a category for businesses that sit where a user meets the payment system: the point at which an account is issued, a transfer is sent onward, a transaction is initiated, or payment data is routed through an acquiring or gateway function. The definition is broad enough to encompass connected payment-service activities, yet precise about their position on the front end. It is not framed as a back-office abstraction; it describes services supplied directly to the end user of the payment system.

The registration picture is notably straightforward at national level. The activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. It is also open across the full stated range of business scales: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. For a founder assessing market entry, that means the record does not place a lower ownership ceiling on a foreign investor nationally, nor reserve the activity to one business-size category.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. This code is not blocked for PMA registration under the province-wide moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The Bali record identifies Large-scale OSS risk as Medium-High/High, which is why the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today; nationally it is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali’s stated moratorium does not close that route for this code.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today, with national foreign ownership open up to 100%.
